chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said:

Verily, Allah, the Mighty and High, created the creation and knew what they would return to. He commanded them and forbade them. Whatever He commanded them of anything, He made for them the way to take it; and whatever He forbade them of anything, He made for them the way to leave it. And they do not take or leave except by the permission of Allah.
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between divine command and human ability in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* articulates the Shia doctrine of *al-Amr bayn al-Amrayn* (the position between the two extremes), rejecting both absolute determinism (*Jabariyya*) and total relinquishment (*Tafwid*). It clarifies that while Allah’s foreknowledge and permission (*idhn*) are the ultimate basis for all actions, humans possess genuine agency to choose between obedience and prohibition, thereby ensuring moral accountability.
